key_insight: The paper replaces Lagrange-multiplier or weak boundary treatments with a lifting-based decomposition that strongly imposes Dirichlet boundary velocities while preserving the port-Hamiltonian energy structure.
engineering_relevance: This gives finite element elastodynamics models an ODE form with better boundary accuracy and a direct link to standard matrix-partitioning practices used in computational mechanics.
method: Split displacement and velocity into a boundary-vanishing dynamic part plus a prescribed lifting field.
Embed the lifting as a distributed port in virtual power formulations to derive lifted port-Hamiltonian models.
Discretize into 2-field and 4-field FEM formulations; standard FEM is recovered under specific shape functions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical simulations showing the proposed method preserves energy-balance properties and performs well computationally.
watch_item: The lifting field and shape-function choices must be implemented carefully, since the discrete equivalence to standard FEM and the quality of boundary enforcement depend on them.
paper_title: Strong imposition of Dirichlet boundary velocities in structure-preserving discretizations of elastodynamics
